title: Checkout domain rules
body: Order placement invariants for APP-003 (Checkout Service): (1) a guest checkout MUST NOT create a Loyalty (APP-015) account; (2) payment authorization (APP-012) precedes inventory commitment (APP-010); (3) all order-placement calls carry an idempotency key (see KN-052).

title: Order-placement idempotency standard
body: All order-placement calls into APP-003 (Checkout Service) and all payment authorization/capture calls into APP-012 (Payments Service) MUST carry a client-generated idempotency key in the 'Idempotency-Key' header (UUIDv4). The receiving service persists the key with the request fingerprint and the first computed result for at least 24 hours. A retry presenting a previously seen key MUST return the original stored result verbatim and MUST NOT re-execute the side effect (no duplicate order, no duplicate charge). A key replayed with a different request body returns HTTP 422. Keys are scoped per endpoint and per customer/cart. This is the enterprise idempotency contract referenced by KN-045.

title: Promotion cache invalidation rule
body: Any pricing or promotion change taking effect during an active promotion window MUST invalidate and refresh the APP-008 (Promotions Engine) promotions cache using write-through semantics: the authoritative store is updated first, then the Redis cache entry is rewritten (not merely evicted) within the same transaction boundary before the change is acknowledged. Cache keys are versioned by promotion id and effective-window; consumers (APP-004 Cart, APP-003 Checkout) must read the current version. A stale promotions cache causes incorrect cart totals and mispriced orders, as seen in INC-2026-007. TTL-only expiry is NOT acceptable for in-window changes.

title: Monetary rounding and currency precision
body: APP-007 (Pricing Service) MUST represent all monetary amounts as integer minor units (cents, pence, centavos) in the currency's ISO 4217 minor-unit scale; floating-point money is prohibited end to end. Line-item prices are stored at full precision and rounded only at display and at order-total computation using banker's rounding (round-half-to-even) to the currency scale. The sum of rounded line items MUST equal the rounded order total via largest-remainder allocation so residual cents are distributed deterministically. Currencies with zero minor units (none in MCG's active set) are handled by scale=0. All amounts carry an explicit ISO 4217 currency code; mixing currencies in a single cart or order is rejected.

title: Regional price resolution and currency binding
body: APP-007 (Pricing Service) resolves the effective price for a (SKU, region, currency, channel) tuple. Each of MCG's seven markets binds to exactly one selling currency: US->USD, CA->CAD, MX->MXN, BR->BRL, GB->GBP, DE->EUR, AU->AUD. A price request MUST specify region code (NA/LATAM/EU/APAC) and country; if no country-specific price override exists, resolution falls back to the region base price, then to the global list price, never to a foreign-currency price. A SKU sellable in a market MUST have a resolvable non-null price in that market's currency or it is treated as not-for-sale there. Prices are never converted at request time via FX; every market price is authored explicitly.

title: Tax-inclusive vs tax-exclusive pricing by region
body: Displayed prices MUST honor regional tax-presentation law. EU markets (GB, DE) and AU display VAT/GST-inclusive prices to consumers; NA markets (US, CA, MX) display tax-exclusive prices with tax calculated and added at checkout; BR displays inclusive prices with tax breakdown. APP-007 (Pricing Service) tags each resolved price with a tax_treatment flag (inclusive|exclusive) derived from region, and APP-003 (Checkout Service) MUST compute order tax consistently with that flag so the customer is never double-taxed or under-taxed. Storefront APP-001 renders the legally required inclusive/exclusive label per market.

title: Price-change effective windows and no retroactive repricing
body: APP-007 (Pricing Service) price changes are scheduled with an explicit effective_from (and optional effective_to) timestamp in UTC. A price applies to a cart based on the price effective at the moment of order placement in APP-003, not at cart creation; carts show a pricing preview that may change. Once an order is placed, its captured prices are immutable and MUST NOT be retroactively repriced by any later price change. Backdating effective_from earlier than now is rejected. Overlapping active price records for the same (SKU, market, channel) are a data-integrity error and MUST be prevented by a uniqueness constraint.

title: Price floor and margin-guard enforcement
body: APP-007 (Pricing Service) MUST reject any resolved sell price (after all automatic markdowns but before promotions) that falls below the SKU's configured price floor, defined as unit cost plus the category minimum-margin percentage. Promotions in APP-008 stacked on top may not drive the customer-effective unit price below the absolute floor (cost * (1 + regulatory_minimum)); if a promotion would breach it, the promotion is capped, not the base price. Any price published at or below unit cost requires an explicit owner-approved loss-leader exception flag with an expiry date. Breaches are logged and alerted to TEAM-007 on-call.

title: Cart line-item quantity caps
body: APP-004 (Cart Service) enforces per-line and per-cart quantity limits: a single line item MAY NOT exceed the SKU's max_order_quantity (default 10, overridable per SKU by APP-005 Catalog), and a cart MAY NOT exceed 100 distinct line items or 500 total units. Restricted SKUs (age-restricted, hazmat, purchase-limited promotional items) carry their own tighter caps that always win. Attempts to exceed a cap clamp the quantity to the maximum and return a structured warning; they never silently succeed. Caps are re-validated at checkout in APP-003 because catalog limits may change while a cart is idle.

title: Cart expiry and abandonment lifecycle
body: APP-004 (Cart Service) carts have a rolling TTL: an active (signed-in) cart persists 30 days from last modification; a guest cart persists 7 days keyed to the anonymous session. On each mutation the TTL is reset. Expired carts are soft-deleted and reservable stock, if any, is released. A cart MUST re-price and re-validate item availability (APP-010) and promotions (APP-008) on load if older than 15 minutes, because prices and stock are volatile. Merging a guest cart into a signed-in cart at login unions line items, summing quantities up to the caps in KN-105 and re-resolving prices.

title: Cart pricing preview is non-binding
body: The totals shown by APP-004 (Cart Service) are a non-binding preview. The authoritative price, tax and promotion computation happens at order placement in APP-003 (Checkout Service). The cart MUST clearly reflect the last-resolved values and their staleness, and MUST NOT be treated by any downstream system as a price commitment. If the checkout-time total differs from the cart preview by more than a configurable threshold (default any increase), APP-003 surfaces the change to the customer for explicit re-confirmation before authorizing payment. This prevents silently charging a total the customer did not see.

title: Payment authorization, capture and PCI boundary
body: APP-012 (Payments Service) is the sole holder of PCI cardholder-data scope; raw PAN MUST NEVER leave APP-012's boundary and MUST NEVER be logged, cached, or forwarded to APP-003, APP-009, APP-024 or the data platform. Upstream systems handle only network tokens or PSP tokens. MCG uses auth-then-capture: authorization reserves funds at checkout; capture occurs on shipment confirmation from APP-009 (OMS). An authorization not captured within 7 days MUST be voided automatically. Every authorization and capture carries the idempotency key from KN-052. All card data at rest is encrypted; access is least-privilege and audited (CANON-001 §4.6).

title: Payment retry and decline handling
body: APP-012 (Payments Service) distinguishes retryable soft declines (issuer timeout, temporary network error, insufficient-funds-retry hints) from hard declines (stolen card, do-not-honor, invalid card). Soft declines MAY be retried with exponential backoff up to 3 attempts within the same authorization idempotency key (KN-052) so the customer is never double-authorized. Hard declines MUST NOT be retried programmatically and are returned to APP-003 with a generic, non-enumerating customer message (never revealing issuer reason codes to the client). Gateway-level PSP failover to a secondary processor is permitted only for connectivity failures, not for business declines.

title: Refund rules and refund-to-original-tender
body: APP-012 (Payments Service) refunds MUST return funds to the original tender used for capture; cross-tender refunds are prohibited except gift-card/store-credit fallback authorized by APP-013 (Wallet). The cumulative refunded amount for an order MUST NOT exceed the total captured amount; partial refunds are tracked against remaining refundable balance. A refund can only be issued against a captured payment; an uncaptured authorization is voided, not refunded. Every refund references the originating return (APP-021/APP-009) or support case (APP-017) and carries an idempotency key so a retried refund does not pay the customer twice.

title: 3-D Secure and strong customer authentication
body: APP-012 (Payments Service) MUST apply 3-D Secure 2.x strong customer authentication (SCA) where mandated: EU/UK markets (GB, DE) require SCA for consumer card payments unless a valid exemption (low-value, low-risk TRA, or trusted-beneficiary) applies. When a 3DS challenge is required, checkout (APP-003) MUST complete the challenge before authorization is treated as valid; a frictionless flow is used when the issuer permits. Liability shift is recorded on the authorization. SCA is not applied to NA markets where it is not required, so as not to add needless friction. All 3DS artifacts stay within the PCI boundary (KN-108); the client only receives challenge redirection, never card data.

title: Inventory available-to-promise (ATP) computation
body: APP-010 (Inventory Service) computes ATP per (SKU, fulfillment node) as on_hand minus open_reservations minus safety_stock, floored at zero, plus inbound quantity whose expected receipt is within the promise horizon. Sellable ATP surfaced to APP-004/APP-003 is the network aggregate across nodes able to serve the customer's region. ATP MUST be derived from the authoritative reservation ledger, never from a cached count alone, and MUST be recomputed on every stock-affecting event (receipt, reservation, release, adjustment) received from APP-011 (WMS) via Kafka. Negative ATP is never exposed; it is clamped to zero and alerted as a reconciliation signal.

title: Inventory reservation and oversell prevention
body: APP-010 (Inventory Service) MUST create a hard reservation against ATP before APP-003 (Checkout Service) commits an order, and the reservation decrement MUST be atomic (conditional update: reserve only if available >= requested) to prevent oversell under concurrency. Per KN-045, payment authorization precedes inventory commit; the reservation is confirmed only after auth succeeds and released if auth fails. Reservations carry a TTL (default 15 minutes for in-flight checkout) and expire back to ATP if the order is not placed. The reservation ledger is the single source of truth; double-reserving the same units for two orders is a Sev2-class defect.

title: Inventory oversell backorder and cancellation policy
body: When physical reconciliation from APP-011 (WMS) reveals negative net availability (oversell) for an already-committed order, APP-010 (Inventory Service) and APP-009 (OMS) MUST resolve it deterministically: allocate remaining units by order-placement timestamp (oldest first); shortfall orders are either backordered (if the SKU permits backorder and inbound is within the promise horizon) or cancelled with automatic full refund via APP-012 and customer notification via APP-023. Silent under-shipment is prohibited. Every oversell event opens a reconciliation record and is reported to TEAM-012 for root-cause.

title: Order state machine invariants
body: APP-009 (OMS) orders traverse a strict state machine: CREATED -> PAYMENT_AUTHORIZED -> ALLOCATED -> PICKING -> SHIPPED -> DELIVERED, with terminal branches CANCELLED and RETURNED. Transitions are one-directional except explicitly defined compensations; illegal transitions (e.g., SHIPPED -> ALLOCATED) MUST be rejected. An order MUST NOT reach ALLOCATED without a confirmed inventory reservation (APP-010) and MUST NOT reach SHIPPED without a successful payment capture (APP-012). Every transition is event-sourced and emitted to Kafka for downstream consumers; the current state is derivable by replay. Cancellation is only permitted before SHIPPED; after that the flow is return/refund.

title: Order split-shipment and partial-fulfillment rules
body: APP-009 (OMS) MAY split an order across multiple fulfillment nodes when no single node can fulfill all lines; each shipment is an independent fulfillment unit with its own tracking, but the order total and tax are computed once at placement and never re-derived per shipment. Payment capture (APP-012) occurs per shipment on dispatch, and the sum of captures MUST NOT exceed the single authorization total. A cancelled line before allocation reduces the capturable amount; the authorization is adjusted or partially voided accordingly. Customers see one order with multiple shipments, not multiple orders.

title: Catalog SKU lifecycle and status transitions
body: APP-005 (Product Catalog) SKUs follow the lifecycle DRAFT -> ACTIVE -> DISCONTINUED -> ARCHIVED. Only ACTIVE SKUs are sellable and indexable by APP-006 (Search). A SKU MUST have a resolvable price (APP-007) and a canonical title, primary image, and category before it can transition to ACTIVE; publishing an incomplete SKU is rejected. DISCONTINUED SKUs remain visible for existing orders and returns but are removed from new-purchase paths; ARCHIVED SKUs are excluded from all customer surfaces. SKU identifiers are immutable and never reused (CANON-001 §6). Catalog changes propagate to consumers via Kafka events with backward-compatible schemas.

title: Catalog offer-price consistency contract
body: APP-005 (Product Catalog) holds offer metadata but is NOT the pricing authority; the sellable price is always resolved from APP-007 (Pricing Service) at read time. Catalog MUST NOT cache or persist a price that can diverge from APP-007. A SKU marked sellable in a market whose price cannot be resolved by APP-007 in that market's currency (KN-101) MUST be treated as not-available in that market rather than displayed priceless or at a stale value. Catalog and Pricing align on SKU keys via the shared contracts registry (TEAM-030); any key drift is a data-contract violation.

title: Promotion stacking and exclusivity rules
body: APP-008 (Promotions Engine) evaluates promotions in a deterministic order and enforces stacking policy: each promotion declares stackable=true|false and a priority. An exclusive (stackable=false) promotion, once applied, blocks all other discounts on the same line or cart per its scope. When multiple exclusive promotions qualify, the one yielding the greatest customer benefit is applied (best-for-customer resolution), ties broken by highest priority then earliest expiry. Order-level and line-level promotions never double-discount the same amount. The final discounted price MUST respect the price floor in KN-104. Evaluation is idempotent for a given cart snapshot so previews and checkout agree.

title: Coupon redemption limits and single-use enforcement
body: APP-008 (Promotions Engine) coupons carry redemption constraints: global redemption cap, per-customer cap (default 1), minimum basket value, and eligible-SKU/category scope. Single-use coupon codes MUST be atomically marked redeemed at order placement (APP-003), keyed to the order and idempotency key (KN-052), so a retried placement does not consume a second redemption and concurrent placements cannot both redeem a one-time code. Expired, exhausted, or out-of-scope coupons are rejected with a specific reason; a coupon applied in the cart but invalid at checkout is removed and the customer is re-prompted. Coupon codes are never guessable-sequential and are rate-limited at the gateway (KN-141).

title: Promotion window scheduling and timezone handling
body: APP-008 (Promotions Engine) promotion windows are stored in UTC with an explicit start and end; activation and deactivation MUST be evaluated against UTC while being presented to customers in the market's local timezone. A promotion is active strictly within [start, end); boundary instants are deterministic. Region-scoped promotions (e.g., a US-only sale) MUST NOT apply to carts resolved for other markets. Scheduling a promotion whose end precedes its start, or that overlaps an exclusive promotion of the same scope, is rejected at authoring time. Any in-window change triggers the cache invalidation in KN-063.

title: Search relevance freshness SLA
body: APP-006 (Search & Browse) MUST reflect catalog and price changes within a bounded freshness SLA: ACTIVE/DISCONTINUED status changes and price changes from APP-005/APP-007 MUST be searchable within 5 minutes (p95) of the emitting Kafka event; new ACTIVE SKUs within 15 minutes. A discontinued or archived SKU (KN-117) MUST disappear from purchasable search results within the same 5-minute window to avoid selling unavailable items. Out-of-stock items (ATP=0 from APP-010) are demoted, not necessarily removed, per merchandising policy. Index lag beyond SLA raises an alert to TEAM-003 and is a candidate Sev3.

title: Search result eligibility and market filtering
body: APP-006 (Search & Browse) MUST filter results to items sellable in the requesting customer's market: a SKU without a resolvable price in the market currency (KN-101) or not ACTIVE (KN-117) MUST NOT appear in purchasable results. Age-restricted or region-restricted SKUs are filtered per the customer's verified region and, where required, age gate. Search MUST NOT leak internal-only fields (cost, margin, supplier) into any customer-facing response. Relevance ranking may personalize ordering but MUST NOT override hard eligibility filters; an ineligible item is never rankable into view.

title: Search query handling and zero-result policy
body: APP-006 (Search & Browse) MUST sanitize and normalize queries (trim, lowercase-fold per locale, strip control characters) and MUST NOT pass raw user input into index queries in a way that permits query injection. Queries are language-aware per market locale (English, Spanish, French-CA, Portuguese, German). A zero-result query MUST return a structured empty result with spelling suggestions and category fallbacks, never an error. Search latency SLO is p95 < 300 ms at the service; breaches degrade gracefully to a cached/basic ranker rather than failing the storefront (APP-001).

title: Catalog event schema backward-compatibility
body: APP-005 (Product Catalog) publishes product and offer change events to Kafka; per CANON-001 §4.8 and §8 these schemas are registered in the schema registry and MUST evolve backward-compatibly. Producers MAY add optional fields but MUST NOT remove or repurpose existing fields, nor tighten types, without a new major event version and a deprecation window coordinated with consumers (APP-006, APP-004, APP-020) through TEAM-030 contracts. Consumers MUST tolerate unknown fields. A breaking change shipped without a versioned migration is a cross-service contract violation blocked by contract tests in CI.

title: Guest checkout data-minimization rule
body: APP-003 (Checkout Service) guest checkout MUST collect only the data required to fulfill and communicate about the order (shipping/billing address, contact email/phone, payment token). Per KN-045 it MUST NOT create a Loyalty (APP-015) account and MUST NOT silently create a full identity (APP-014) profile; any account creation is an explicit, opt-in post-purchase action. Guest PII is classified pii and retained only as long as needed for the order lifecycle plus the legal returns/tax window, then minimized. Marketing consent is never assumed from a guest purchase; opt-in is explicit.

title: Checkout address validation and shippability
body: APP-003 (Checkout Service) MUST validate and normalize the shipping address against the market's address format and MUST confirm the destination is serviceable for every line item before authorizing payment. Items with region restrictions (hazmat, age-restricted, export-controlled) that cannot ship to the destination MUST block placement with a specific per-item reason, not a generic failure. Tax jurisdiction is derived from the validated shipping address (KN-102). A checkout MUST NOT authorize payment (APP-012) for an order it cannot fulfill; shippability and reservation (APP-010) checks precede the payment step per KN-045.

title: Checkout latency SLO and graceful degradation
body: APP-003 (Checkout Service) order-placement API has a p99 latency SLO of 1200 ms and p50 of 300 ms measured at the gateway (APP-024). When a non-critical dependency degrades (e.g., APP-008 Promotions), checkout MUST degrade gracefully by proceeding with last-known-good promotion state within its freshness bound rather than failing placement, EXCEPT where correctness requires the dependency (payment authorization APP-012 and inventory reservation APP-010 are non-bypassable). Circuit breakers protect each downstream call with bounded timeouts and no unbounded retries (see KN-052 for idempotent retry behavior). SLO breaches during progressive rollout trigger automated rollback (CANON-001 §7.4).

title: Returns eligibility policy
body: APP-021 (Customer Portal) self-service returns MUST enforce eligibility before issuing an RMA: the item is within the return window (default 30 days from delivery, 90 days for Loyalty higher tiers, 14 days for final-sale categories), the order reached DELIVERED (APP-009 state, KN-115), and the SKU category is returnable (perishables, digital goods, and hygiene items are non-returnable unless defective). Return quantity MUST NOT exceed the delivered quantity. An approved return creates a return record in APP-009 and, on receipt/inspection at APP-011 (WMS), triggers a refund to original tender per KN-110. Ineligible requests are declined with a specific reason and a support handoff to APP-017.

title: Customer portal authorization scoping
body: APP-021 (Customer Portal) MUST enforce that an authenticated customer can view and act only on their own orders, addresses, payment instruments, and loyalty balance; every read and mutation is authorized against the identity from APP-014 (Identity) and the resource owner. Insecure direct object reference (accessing another customer's order by guessing an id) MUST be impossible; order and return identifiers are non-sequential and access-checked server-side, never trusted from the client. Payment instrument display shows only tokenized last-four; full PAN is never retrievable (KN-108). Portal never exposes internal fulfillment, cost, or fraud-scoring data.

title: Return refund timing and restocking rules
body: For an approved return (KN-129), APP-009 (OMS) MUST NOT release the refund via APP-012 until the returned item is received and passes inspection at APP-011 (WMS), except for policy-defined instant-refund cases (low-value items or high-trust Loyalty tiers) which refund on carrier scan. Restockable items in sellable condition return to ATP (APP-010) at the receiving node; damaged/defective items are quarantined and never restocked. The refund amount equals the returned line value plus applicable tax, minus non-refundable fees per policy, and MUST NOT exceed the captured amount for those lines (KN-110). Refund status is visible to the customer in APP-021 and to agents in APP-017.

title: Loyalty points accrual rules
body: Loyalty (APP-015, Meridian Rewards) accrues points only on captured, net-of-returns spend: points are provisionally granted at order placement and become redeemable after the return window closes for the order (KN-129), or are clawed back proportionally on refund. Accrual excludes taxes, shipping, gift-card purchases, and the discounted portion funded by promotions; it accrues on the customer-paid amount. Guest orders accrue nothing (KN-045). Accrual rate is tier-dependent and configured per market; points have no cash value and are non-transferable. Every accrual/clawback references the originating order (APP-009) and is idempotent so replayed order events do not double-grant points.

title: Loyalty redemption and balance integrity
body: Loyalty (APP-015) redemptions MUST atomically debit the point ledger with a conditional update (redeem only if balance >= requested) to prevent negative balances and concurrent double-spend. Points redeemed for a discount at checkout (APP-003) are held while the order is in flight and are committed on capture or released on cancellation/auth failure, mirroring the reservation pattern in KN-113. Expired points are removed by a scheduled, auditable job and cannot be redeemed after expiry. The ledger is append-only and every entry references its source event; the current balance is always derivable by replay and MUST reconcile to the ledger.

title: Storefront price and availability display consistency
body: APP-001 (Storefront Web) MUST display the price resolved from APP-007 (KN-101) and availability from APP-010, never a client-cached or hardcoded value, and MUST render the legally required tax-inclusive/exclusive label per market (KN-102). When a product is not sellable in the visitor's market it MUST show an appropriate unavailable state rather than a broken or zero price. The 'add to cart' action MUST re-validate price and availability server-side; the storefront never authoritatively computes totals. Storefront MUST NOT expose internal identifiers, cost, or margin, and MUST degrade to a read-only browse experience if checkout dependencies are down rather than showing errors.

title: Storefront localization and market routing
body: APP-001 (Storefront Web) MUST route each visitor to the correct market context (region code NA/LATAM/EU/APAC, country, currency, language) and keep that context consistent across catalog, search, cart, and checkout for the whole session. Supported locales are US-en/es, CA-en/fr, MX-es, BR-pt, GB-en, DE-de, AU-en (CANON-001 §1.4). Currency, price presentation, and legal copy (returns, tax, cookie/consent) MUST match the selected market. Switching market re-resolves prices and re-validates the cart (KN-106); it MUST NOT carry a foreign-currency price across markets.

title: API Gateway authentication and mTLS policy
body: APP-024 (API Gateway / Edge) is the single ingress for external traffic and MUST authenticate every request before routing: consumer traffic via OAuth2/OIDC tokens validated against APP-014 (Identity), and all internal service-to-service calls via mutual TLS with least-privilege workload identity (CANON-001 §4.6). Unauthenticated requests to protected routes are rejected with 401 at the edge; the gateway MUST NOT forward unauthenticated traffic to backends. PCI cardholder data never traverses the gateway in the clear and card fields are never logged (KN-108). The gateway terminates TLS, enforces allowed methods, and injects a correlation/trace id (CANON-001 §8 Observability) on every request.

title: API versioning and deprecation policy
body: Per CANON-001 §4.8, all external APIs behind APP-024 (API Gateway) are versioned in the URL path (/v1/...); backward-incompatible changes REQUIRE a new major version and MUST NOT be shipped by mutating an existing version's contract. A deprecated version MUST remain available for a minimum 90-day deprecation window with Sunset/Deprecation response headers announcing the removal date, and consumers MUST be notified through the contracts registry (TEAM-030). REST resources are plural nouns; responses use the shared error envelope and pagination conventions. Removing a version before its window elapses is prohibited.

title: Gateway idempotency and safe-retry propagation
body: APP-024 (API Gateway / Edge) MUST propagate the client Idempotency-Key header unchanged to backends and MUST NOT itself retry non-idempotent methods (POST/PATCH on order/payment endpoints) on upstream timeout, because a blind retry can create duplicate orders or charges. Automatic edge retries are permitted only for idempotent, safe methods (GET/HEAD) and for explicitly idempotent endpoints that honor KN-052. Retried requests preserve the original correlation id for traceability. This rule complements the service-side idempotency contract (KN-052) and the checkout latency policy (KN-128).

title: Identity session and token lifetime policy
body: Consumer authentication via APP-014 (Identity) issues short-lived access tokens (default 15 minutes) and longer-lived refresh tokens (default 30 days, rotating on use) over OIDC/OAuth2. Access tokens MUST be validated at APP-024 (Gateway) on every request (KN-136); refresh-token reuse after rotation MUST invalidate the token family (replay detection). Step-up authentication is required for sensitive actions (adding a payment instrument, changing email, high-value redemption). Sessions MUST be revocable centrally (logout-everywhere), and password/credential material is never logged. Failed-login attempts are rate-limited and lock out after a threshold to resist credential stuffing.

title: Customer PII handling and data-subject rights
body: Customer personal data managed by APP-014 (Identity) and surfaced by APP-021 (Customer Portal) is classified pii and MUST be encrypted at rest and in transit, access-controlled least-privilege, and never emitted to logs or analytics without tokenization/pseudonymization. MCG MUST honor data-subject access and erasure requests across the systems that hold PII (APP-014, APP-021, APP-009, APP-016), except where retention is legally mandated (tax/financial records for the statutory period). Erasure anonymizes rather than breaks referential integrity of order history required for accounting. Cross-border personal data handling respects each market's applicable regime (e.g., UK/EU GDPR, Brazil LGPD).

title: Gateway rate-limiting and abuse protection
body: APP-024 (API Gateway / Edge) MUST enforce tiered rate limits: per-authenticated-user, per-IP for anonymous traffic, and per-API-key for partner/seller integrations, with limits calibrated per endpoint sensitivity. Sensitive endpoints (login and token via APP-014, coupon validation via APP-008, checkout via APP-003) carry stricter limits and progressive backoff to resist brute force, coupon enumeration (KN-120) and credential stuffing (KN-139). Exceeding a limit returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header and is never silently dropped. Limits are enforced at the edge before backend load is incurred; bursts are absorbed with a token-bucket. Rate-limit events feed observability and security dashboards (TEAM-032/TEAM-040).

title: Kafka event schema and ordering guarantees
body: All domain events across the commerce path (order, inventory, payment, catalog, promotion) are published to Kafka with schemas registered in the schema registry and evolved backward-compatibly (CANON-001 §4.8, §8). Events for a single aggregate (e.g., one order id, one SKU-node) MUST be partitioned by the aggregate key to preserve per-key ordering; consumers MUST be idempotent and tolerate at-least-once delivery and duplicate redelivery. Events carry an event id, aggregate id, version, and UTC timestamp. Consumers MUST NOT assume global ordering across keys. A poison message MUST route to a dead-letter topic with alerting, never block the partition indefinitely.

title: Promotion best-deal computation determinism
body: APP-008 (Promotions Engine) MUST produce the same discount result for the same cart snapshot and evaluation timestamp regardless of node, thread, or evaluation order (deterministic and referentially transparent). All eligible-promotion resolution, best-for-customer selection (KN-119) and tie-breaks MUST be pure functions of inputs; no wall-clock, random, or cache-order dependence may affect the outcome. This determinism is what allows the cart preview (KN-107) and the checkout-time recomputation (APP-003) to agree, and is a precondition for reliable evaluation/benchmarking of AI-authored promotion changes.

title: Tax calculation and jurisdiction rules by market
body: Order tax in APP-003 (Checkout Service) is computed per the destination jurisdiction derived from the validated shipping address (KN-127): US/CA use destination-based sales tax / GST+PST by province and locality; MX applies IVA; BR applies its layered consumption taxes; GB and DE apply VAT; AU applies GST. Tax is computed on the discounted, customer-paid amount after promotions, never on the pre-discount price, and shipping is taxed where the jurisdiction requires it. Tax-inclusive markets (KN-102) back out the tax component for reporting. Captured order tax is immutable post-placement; corrections are handled via refund/adjustment, not by mutating the order.

title: Inventory safety-stock and node-selection policy
body: APP-010 (Inventory Service) reserves a configurable safety-stock buffer per (SKU, node) that is excluded from ATP (KN-112) to absorb count drift and prevent oversell during high-velocity sales and promotion windows. Node selection for fulfillment MUST prefer the node minimizing split shipments and delivery time to the customer's region while respecting node capacity and cutoff times, coordinated with APP-009 (KN-116). Safety-stock levels are raised automatically ahead of known peak windows (peak-readiness) and are never set to zero for Tier 0 checkout-path SKUs without owner approval. Physical counts from APP-011 (WMS) reconcile the ledger on a defined cadence.

title: Peak-readiness change-freeze and load policy
body: During designated peak windows (major promotional events and seasonal peaks), Tier 0 commerce-path services (APP-003, APP-004, APP-007, APP-010, APP-012, APP-024) enter a change-freeze: only incident hotfixes (CANON-001 §7.3) and pre-approved changes deploy, and every such change requires the elevated Tier 0/PCI approvals (CANON-001 §7.5). Services MUST have validated capacity against forecast peak load with headroom (performance tests per CANON-001 §4.4), circuit breakers and graceful degradation (KN-128) verified, and promotion caches pre-warmed (KN-063). Autoscaling limits and rate-limit budgets (KN-141) are raised for the window and reverted after. The freeze is coordinated by the Architecture Office (TEAM-090) with SRE (TEAM-032).
